text: With a fair wind and an early start it should be only one day’s sail of about sixty miles. “The plan only came to a head on the evening of the third day, on the 12th of September. “I told you, I think, that the weather had broken after a long spell of heat. That very day it had been blowing pretty hard from the west, and the glass was falling still. I said, of course, that I couldn’t go with him if the weather was too bad, but he prophesied a good day, said it was an easy sail, and altogether put me on my mettle.
